\section{Introduction}

Multi-judge panels have emerged as the dominant defense against bias and manipulation in LLM-based evaluation. After \citet{zheng2023judging} demonstrated that individual LLM judges can rival human annotators, subsequent work revealed systematic vulnerabilities: position bias, verbosity preferences, and sycophancy compromise the reliability of any single judge \citep{wang2023fair}. The natural response has been to aggregate decisions across diverse models, drawing on an implicit analogy to Byzantine fault tolerance (BFT), where majority voting among $n$ independent nodes tolerates up to $f < n/3$ faulty members \citep{lamport1982byzantine,castro1999practical}. A recent systematization of LLM-judge security reinforces this assumption, reporting that 7-model committees reduce attack success rates from 50--68\% to 10--19\% \citep{almasoud2026security}. Diversity, by this logic, is the key ingredient for secure evaluation.

Yet the evidence for diversity as a causal defense mechanism is weaker than it appears. The observed ASR reduction in multi-judge panels \citep{almasoud2026security} conflates two distinct factors: the diversity of the panel (how independently judges respond to attacks) and the individual robustness of the strongest members. No existing work disentangles these contributions. The theoretical justification rests on similarly uncertain ground: the strong data-processing inequality (SDPI) bounds joint failure in terms of effective independence, but assumes non-adaptive faults. BFT guarantees tolerate arbitrary failures up to a threshold count, yet do not model adversaries that observe panel composition and strategically select attacks \citep{schneier2000secrets}. When the threat shifts from random noise to adaptive manipulation, the assumptions underlying the diversity defense no longer hold.

Adding more diverse judges to an evaluation panel predominantly increases, rather than decreases, vulnerability to adversarial manipulation. The reversal mechanism is straightforward. Under random faults, independent judges fail via uncorrelated events, and majority voting aggregates away individual errors. Under an adaptive adversary, the picture inverts: functionally diverse judges respond to different manipulation strategies, and an adversary who observes the panel can exploit judge-specific vulnerabilities across a broader space of attacks \citep{goodfellow2015adversarial,papernot2016transferability}. Diversity ceases to provide mutual protection and instead expands the viable attack surface. We call this the \emph{diversity trap}: the same property that reduces vulnerability under random faults increases it under strategic attack.

Controlled experiments across 15 models from 6 families, 455 panels, 6 attack types, and 2 benchmarks (MMLU, ARC) confirm that diversity predominantly increases vulnerability: $K_{\mathrm{eff}}$, a pairwise-MI-based diversity metric, is a significant positive predictor of panel attack success rate in 7 of 12 conditions, non-significant in 4, and significantly \emph{negative} in 1 (sycophancy on ARC, where diverse panels dilute a shared cognitive bias). The weakest-judge channel $\eta_{\max}$ is significant in 11 of 12 conditions. Dominance analysis reveals condition-dependent patterns: $\eta_{\max}$ is the sole dominant predictor in 4 conditions, both drivers are co-dominant in 7, and $K_{\mathrm{eff}}$ alone dominates in 1 condition (position bias on ARC). The sycophancy exception is mechanistically informative: when the attack exploits a bias shared across all judges, diverse panels dilute that bias---precisely the regime where the BFT analogy holds.

These findings yield three contributions:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Diversity trap and dual vulnerability drivers.} The first empirical quantification showing that panel diversity ($K_{\mathrm{eff}}$) predominantly and independently predicts vulnerability under adaptive attack (7 of 12 conditions), across 15 models, 455 panels, and dominance analysis that isolates each driver's contribution (\S\ref{sec:experiments}).
\item \textbf{BFT reversal mechanism.} Formal and empirical demonstration of why diversity helps under random faults but hurts under adaptive adversaries, with condition-dependent importance patterns that reveal when each vulnerability channel dominates (\S\ref{sec:threat_model}, \S\ref{sec:analysis}).
\item \textbf{Robustness-first panel design.} An actionable defense combining robustness screening with reliability-weighted aggregation that addresses both vulnerability channels (\S\ref{sec:analysis}).
\end{enumerate}

1	\section{Experimental Methodology}
2	\label{sec:experiments}
3	
4	\subsection{Models and Panel Construction}
5	
6	We select 15 LLM judges spanning 5 provider families and 3 capability tiers, listed in Table~\ref{tab:models}. Nine models are accessed via the OpenRouter API; six open-weight models are served locally using vLLM~0.21.0 with AWQ INT4 quantization on an NVIDIA RTX~6000 (96\,GB). Capability tiers are assigned by mean clean accuracy across both benchmarks: \emph{frontier} (top 5), \emph{mid-tier} (middle 5), and \emph{lightweight} (bottom 5). All panels consist of $K{=}3$ judges with majority-vote threshold $t{=}2$. Exhaustive enumeration yields $\binom{15}{3} = 455$ unique panels, covering every combination of families and tiers. Each panel evaluates all benchmark items under all attack types, producing a complete panel $\times$ item $\times$ attack tensor.
7	
8	\begin{table}[t]
9	\centering
10	\small
11	\begin{tabular}{llll}
12	\toprule
13	\textbf{Model} & \textbf{Family} & \textbf{Tier} & \textbf{Deploy} \\
14	\midrule
15	gpt-5.5              & OpenAI    & frontier    & API \\
16	gpt-4.1              & OpenAI    & frontier    & API \\
17	gpt-4.1-mini          & OpenAI    & mid-tier    & API \\
18	gpt-4.1-nano          & OpenAI    & lightweight & API \\
19	claude-opus-4-6       & Anthropic & frontier    & API \\
20	claude-sonnet-4-6     & Anthropic & mid-tier    & API \\
21	claude-3-haiku        & Anthropic & lightweight & API \\
22	gemini-3.1-pro-preview & Google   & frontier    & API \\
23	gemini-3.5-flash      & Google    & mid-tier    & API \\
24	qwen2.5-32b           & Qwen      & mid-tier    & local \\
25	qwen2.5-14b           & Qwen      & lightweight & local \\
26	llama-3.1-8b          & Llama     & lightweight & local \\
27	\emph{[3 local models TBD]} & --- & --- & local \\
28	\bottomrule
29	\end{tabular}
30	\caption{Judge models used in the study. API models accessed via OpenRouter; local models served with vLLM + AWQ INT4 quantization. Tier assignment is based on mean clean accuracy across MMLU and ARC.}
31	\label{tab:models}
32	\end{table}
33	
34	\subsection{Benchmarks and Attack Types}
35	
36	Two benchmarks test distinct evaluation capabilities: MMLU \citep{hendrycks2021mmlu}, a knowledge-intensive multiple-choice benchmark spanning 57 subjects, and ARC \citep{clark2018arc}, a reasoning-intensive science question benchmark. We sample 300 items from each benchmark. MMLU probes factual recall and broad domain knowledge; ARC requires multi-step scientific reasoning. All API calls use temperature~0 for deterministic outputs; local models are served with the same temperature setting. Attacked variants are generated by programmatically applying each manipulation to the candidate text, with a fixed random seed for reproducibility.
37	
38	Each benchmark is paired with six attack types that target different judge vulnerabilities: (1)~\textbf{prompt injection}, adversarial instructions embedded in candidate text that override the evaluation prompt \citep{perez2022ignore,greshake2023not}; (2)~\textbf{sycophancy}, responses engineered to agree with or flatter the judge \citep{wang2023fair}; (3)~\textbf{score manipulation}, explicit numerical cues (e.g., ``this answer deserves a 10/10'') injected into the candidate to anchor scoring; (4)~\textbf{verbosity bias}, padding correct answers with excessive irrelevant detail to exploit length preferences \citep{zheng2023judging}; (5)~\textbf{position bias}, reordering candidate answers to place the target in the position judges systematically favor \citep{wang2023fair}; and (6)~\textbf{authority bias}, prefacing candidate text with fabricated credentials or citations to inflate perceived credibility. The combination of 2 benchmarks and 6 attacks produces 12 experimental conditions, each evaluated across all 455 panels.
39	
40	\subsection{Vulnerability Metrics}
41	
42	Per-judge vulnerability under attack $a$ is the fraction of items where judge $j$ is fooled: $\eta_j(a) = \Pr(X_j^a {=} 1)$, estimated empirically over the item set. The weakest-link vulnerability $\eta_{\max}(a) = \max_{j \in \mathcal{P}} \eta_j(a)$ captures the most susceptible member of each panel. The panel attack success rate $\mathrm{ASR}(\mathcal{P}, a)$ is the fraction of items where at least $t$ judges are simultaneously fooled. Panel diversity is quantified by $K_{\mathrm{eff}}$ (Equation~\ref{eq:keff}), computed from pairwise mutual information between judges' three-category winner labels (model~A wins, model~B wins, tie) on clean (unattacked) data. MI is estimated via the plug-in estimator with Miller--Madow bias correction. In practice, $K_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is computed through the Gaussian copula correlation matrix: under the Gaussian assumption, pairwise MI and copula $\rho$ are related by $\mathrm{MI} = -\tfrac{1}{2}\log(1-\rho^2)$ \citep{nelsen2006copulas}, and we substitute $\exp(-2\,\mathrm{MI}) = 1 - \rho^2$ directly into Equation~\ref{eq:keff}. Together, $\eta_{\max}$ and $K_{\mathrm{eff}}$ serve as the two predictors in the regression framework below: $\eta_{\max}$ indexes the weakest-link channel and $K_{\mathrm{eff}}$ indexes the diversity channel.
43	
44	\subsection{Aggregation Methods}
45	
46	Beyond the default majority vote, we evaluate three alternative aggregation rules to test whether the diversity trap persists under different decision mechanisms. The aggregation comparison uses the same log-log regression specification as the primary analysis (Equation~\ref{eq:regression}).
47	
48	\paragraph{Majority Vote.} Accept if $\sum_{j=1}^K \mathbf{1}[J_j \text{ approves}] \geq \lceil K/2 \rceil$. This is the standard baseline aggregation assumed throughout the main analysis.
49	
50	\paragraph{Accuracy-Weighted Vote.} Accept if $\sum_{j=1}^K w_j \cdot \mathbf{1}[J_j \text{ approves}] > 0.5$, where $w_j \propto \mathrm{acc}_j$ on held-out clean data, normalized so that $\sum_j w_j = 1$. Judges with higher clean-data accuracy receive proportionally greater influence.
51	
52	\paragraph{Threshold Vote (Unanimity).} Accept only if all $K$ judges approve ($t = K$). A single dissenting judge suffices to reject, making this the most conservative rule.
53	
54	\paragraph{Bayesian Calibration.} Compute $P(\text{correct} \mid \mathbf{v}) \propto P(\text{correct}) \prod_j P(v_j \mid \text{correct})$, where $P(v_j \mid \cdot)$ is derived from judge $j$'s confusion matrix on clean data and $\mathbf{v}$ is the observed vote vector. Accept if the posterior exceeds 0.5. This rule uses each judge's calibrated reliability rather than treating all votes equally.
55	
56	\subsection{Statistical Framework}
57	\label{sec:stat_framework}
58	
59	To disentangle the contributions of panel diversity and individual judge robustness, we fit a log-log OLS regression for each of the 12 conditions:
60	\begin{equation}
61	\label{eq:regression}
62	\log(\mathrm{ASR} + \epsilon) = \alpha + \beta_1 \log(K_{\mathrm{eff}}) + \beta_2 \log(\eta_{\max} + \epsilon),
63	\end{equation}
64	with $\epsilon = 10^{-6}$ to handle zero values. Standardized coefficients $\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{std}} = \hat{\beta} \cdot \mathrm{SD}(\log x) / \mathrm{SD}(\log y)$ enable direct comparison of effect magnitudes across predictors and conditions. We apply Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multiple testing, controlling the false discovery rate per predictor across the 12 conditions.
65	
66	To assess relative predictor importance beyond regression coefficients, we perform dominance analysis \citep{budescu1993dominance}. This method decomposes $R^2$ by averaging each predictor's incremental $R^2$ contribution across all possible subsets of predictors. A predictor is \emph{dominant} if its average contribution exceeds that of the competing predictor in every subset ordering. With two predictors, dominance reduces to comparing each predictor's solo $R^2$ with its incremental $R^2$ conditional on the other.
67	
68	\subsection{Sensitivity Analysis}
69	
70	Judges with clean-data accuracy below 0.5 perform at or below chance and could drive regression results through extreme outlier behavior rather than meaningful vulnerability patterns. We exclude such judges from panel construction and re-run the log-log regression (Equation~\ref{eq:regression}) to verify that the $K_{\mathrm{eff}}$ effect remains stable after removing these potential confounds.

\section{Introduction}

Multi-judge panels have emerged as the dominant defense against bias and manipulation in LLM-based evaluation. After \citet{zheng2023judging} demonstrated that individual LLM judges can rival human annotators, subsequent work revealed systematic vulnerabilities: position bias, verbosity preferences, and sycophancy compromise the reliability of any single judge \citep{wang2023fair}. The natural response has been to aggregate decisions across diverse models, drawing on an implicit analogy to Byzantine fault tolerance (BFT), where majority voting among $n$ independent nodes tolerates up to $f < n/3$ faulty members \citep{lamport1982byzantine,castro1999practical}. A recent systematization of LLM-judge security reinforces this assumption, reporting that 7-model committees reduce attack success rates from 50--68\% to 10--19\% \citep{almasoud2026security}. Diversity, by this logic, is the key ingredient for secure evaluation.

Yet the evidence for diversity as a causal defense mechanism is weaker than it appears. The observed ASR reduction in multi-judge panels \citep{almasoud2026security} conflates two distinct factors: the diversity of the panel (how independently judges respond to attacks) and the individual robustness of the strongest members. No existing work disentangles these contributions. The theoretical justification rests on similarly uncertain ground: the strong data-processing inequality (SDPI) bounds joint failure in terms of effective independence, but assumes non-adaptive faults. BFT guarantees tolerate arbitrary failures up to a threshold count, yet do not model adversaries that observe panel composition and strategically select attacks \citep{schneier2000secrets}. When the threat shifts from random noise to adaptive manipulation, the assumptions underlying the diversity defense no longer hold.

Adding more diverse judges to an evaluation panel predominantly increases, rather than decreases, vulnerability to adversarial manipulation. The reversal mechanism is straightforward. Under random faults, independent judges fail via uncorrelated events, and majority voting aggregates away individual errors. Under an adaptive adversary, the picture inverts: functionally diverse judges respond to different manipulation strategies, and an adversary who observes the panel can exploit judge-specific vulnerabilities across a broader space of attacks \citep{goodfellow2015adversarial,papernot2016transferability}. Diversity ceases to provide mutual protection and instead expands the viable attack surface. We call this the \emph{diversity trap}: the same property that reduces vulnerability under random faults increases it under strategic attack.

Controlled experiments across 15 models from 5 families, 455 panels, 6 attack types, and 2 benchmarks (MMLU, ARC) confirm that diversity predominantly increases vulnerability: $K_{\mathrm{eff}}$, a pairwise-MI-based diversity metric, is a significant positive predictor of panel attack success rate in 7 of 12 conditions, non-significant in 4, and significantly \emph{negative} in 1 (sycophancy on ARC, where diverse panels dilute a shared cognitive bias). The weakest-judge channel $\eta_{\max}$ is significant in 11 of 12 conditions. Dominance analysis reveals condition-dependent patterns: $\eta_{\max}$ is the sole dominant predictor in 4 conditions, both drivers are co-dominant in 7, and $K_{\mathrm{eff}}$ alone dominates in 1 condition (position bias on ARC). The sycophancy exception is mechanistically informative: when the attack exploits a bias shared across all judges, diverse panels dilute that bias---precisely the regime where the BFT analogy holds.

These findings yield three contributions:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Diversity trap and dual vulnerability drivers.} The first empirical quantification showing that panel diversity ($K_{\mathrm{eff}}$) predominantly and independently predicts vulnerability under adaptive attack (7 of 12 conditions), across 15 models, 455 panels, and dominance analysis that isolates each driver's contribution (\S\ref{sec:experiments}).
\item \textbf{BFT reversal mechanism.} Formal and empirical demonstration of why diversity helps under random faults but hurts under adaptive adversaries, with condition-dependent importance patterns that reveal when each vulnerability channel dominates (\S\ref{sec:threat_model}, \S\ref{sec:analysis}).
\item \textbf{Robustness-first panel design.} An actionable defense combining robustness screening with reliability-weighted aggregation that addresses both vulnerability channels (\S\ref{sec:analysis}).
\end{enumerate}

55	  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度

57	- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文
58	
59	---
60	
61	## 二、Abstract 写作规范
62	
63	### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）
64	
65	Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
66	1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
67	2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
68	3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
69	4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献
70	
71	### 2.2 禁忌
72	
73	- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
74	- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
75	- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
76	- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
77	- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开
78	
79	### 2.3 审稿人视角检验
80	
81	写完后用这个标准自检：审稿人能否在 30 秒内判断——
82	- 问题是否重要？
83	- 方法是否清楚？
84	- 贡献是否可信？
85	- 结果是否有说服力？
86	
87	---
88	
89	## 三、Introduction 写作规范
90	
91	### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）
92	
93	Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：
94	
95	1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
96	2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
97	3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
98	4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
99	5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献
100	
101	### 3.2 整体叙事结构
102	
103	```
104	现有进展 → 关键缺口 → 本文洞察 → 方法概述 → 实验证据 → 贡献总结
105	```
106	
107	### 3.3 禁忌
108	
109	- **禁止泛泛介绍**：不要开头就写 "LLMs have shown remarkable capabilities..."，要从具体问题切入
110	- **禁止缺少过渡**：每段之间必须有逻辑连接
111	- **禁止实验报告风格**：Introduction 不是 "我们做了 X 实验得到了 Y 结果" 的罗列
112	- 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
113	- Contribution 列表中不能出现未在前文铺垫过的概念
114	
115	---
116	
117	## 四、Related Work 写作规范
118	
119	### 4.1 目标
120	
121	让审稿人相信：作者理解这个领域，知道自己的方法站在什么位置，清楚相对已有工作的真实增量在哪里。
122	
123	### 4.2 结构要求
124	
125	- 把已有工作分成几个清晰的主题（如模型训练、推理增强、工具调用、数据构建、评测等）
126	- 每类简要说明：已有方法做了什么、解决了哪些问题、和本文的关系
127	- 帮助读者理解：哪些是本文直接继承的，哪些方法不同但解决相似问题，哪些留下了本文要解决的缺口
128	
129	### 4.3 禁忌
130	
131	- **禁止论文堆砌**：不要写成 "A proposed X. B proposed Y. C proposed Z." 的列表
132	- **目标不是展示读了多少论文**，而是做归纳和比较
133	- Contribution claim（"To our knowledge, no prior work..."）应放在 Introduction，不在 Related Work
134	
135	### 4.4 引用充足度
136	
137	- 引用必须覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**
138	- 任何一类缺失，审稿人会立刻看出来调研不充分
139	- 引用密度参照目标会议近年录用论文的量级——明显偏少意味着 Related Work 调研不足
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 五、去 AI 写作风格（硬规则）
144	
145	以下模式是 AI 生成文本的典型标志，审稿人一眼能看出。**必须全部消除。**
146	
147	### 5.1 严禁破折号（最显著的 AI 痕迹）
148	
149	**这是 AI 写作最容易被识别的标志，审稿人最敏感。单列为最高优先级硬规则。**
150	
151	- 解释性 em-dash（—，U+2014）和 en-dash（–，U+2013）必须**全部删除**
152	- 替代方式：用逗号、括号或拆分为两个句子
153	- 强制检查命令：
154	  ```bash
155	  grep -n "—" paper/*.tex     # em-dash，每处人工判断是否必要
156	  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
157	  ```
158	- 例外（允许保留）：表格分隔符、数字范围（`2020–2024`、`pp. 12–18`）、专有名词（`Newton–Raphson`）
159	
160	### 5.2 段落与句式
161	
162	- **禁止过度分段**：不需要每 2-3 句就换段，自然段 5-8 句是正常的
163	- **减少关系从句**（which, that, who）：能用简洁直接的句子就不用从句
164	- **禁止 -ing 短语结尾**：如 "..., highlighting the applicability of..." / "..., demonstrating the effectiveness of..."。这是 AI 写作最典型的标志之一
165	- **禁止连续使用 "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally"**：一段内最多用一个过渡词
166	- **避免 "It is worth noting that..." / "Notably, ..."**：直接写要说的内容
167	
168	### 5.3 用词黑名单
169	
170	- 避免 "delve into" / "leverage" / "utilize" / "facilitate" — 用 "explore" / "use" / "enable"
171	- 避免 "a myriad of" / "a plethora of" — 用 "many" / "various"
172	- 避免 "in the realm of" / "in the context of" — 直接说
173	- 避免 "paradigm shift" / "novel" 过度使用
174	
175	### 5.4 校对清单（4 步）
176	
177	1. 全文 proofread 语法和拼写
178	2. 检查所有代词/指示词（this, that, it）是否指代明确
179	3. **`grep "—"` + `grep " – "` 全文清零**（删除所有解释性 dash，§5.1）
180	4. `grep "ing,"` 模式——大部分 -ing 分词短语需要改写
181	
182	---
183	
184	## 六、图表与视觉规范
185	
186	### 6.1 知识密度原则
187	
188	- **图表的信息必须紧凑**——不能为了美观而留大量白空间
189	- 一张图如果只传达一个简单信息，要么缩小要么合并到其他图中
190	- 能用 inline text 说清的不要占一整个 Figure
191	
192	### 6.2 表格规范
193	
194	- 表格和正文文字不能视觉重叠（检查 column 宽度和 alignment）
195	- 小数精度全表统一
196	- 最优加粗、次优下划线
197	- Caption 必须自包含
198	
199	### 6.3 图片规范
200	
201	- 数值标签不能被线、bar、点遮住——用白色背景或偏移标签
202	- 图中字体 >= 7pt（打印后仍可读）
203	- 栏宽约束需匹配目标 venue 模板要求
204	- 概念图/流程图要有信息量，不要画一个 trivial 的 pipeline 然后占半页
205	
206	### 6.4 空间效率
207	
208	- 顶会正文页数严格受限（具体页数查目标会议官网），每 cm² 都是宝贵资源
209	- 优先使用 `\subfigure` 合并相关图
210	- Table 能 inline 就不要单独浮动
211	- 图表占比与其对叙事的贡献成正比
212	
213	### 6.5 页面节奏
214	
215	好论文的页面有节奏感——text、equation、figure 交替出现，读者视觉不疲劳：
216	
217	- **text-equation-figure 三重奏**：重要概念用"文字解释 → 公式定义 → 图表直觉"三步展开
218	- 连续 2 页纯文本（无 figure/equation/table）→ 穿插一个 display item 打破节奏
219	- 连续 2 个 figure 页（整页被 float 占满）→ 至少隔 1 段文字再放下一个 float
220	- Section heading 不孤悬页底（heading 后至少跟 2 行正文，否则强制分页）
221	- 最后一页内容 ≥ 2/3 页面高度（太空显得凑数，太满放不下 references）
222	
223	### 6.6 表格 LaTeX 规范
224	
225	**Booktabs 标准（硬规则）**：
226	- 用 `\toprule` / `\midrule` / `\bottomrule`，禁止 `\hline`，禁止竖线 `|`
227	- 用 `\centering` 不用 `\begin{center}`（后者多加垂直空白）
228	- 最优结果加粗（`\textbf{}`），次优下划线（`\underline{}`）+ 方向箭头 `↑`/`↓` 标明指标方向
229	- 小数精度全表统一（如全部保留 1 位或 2 位）
230	- Caption 在表格上方（`\caption` 在 `\begin{tabular}` 之前）
231	
232	**宽度决策树**：
233	- ≤5 列 → 单栏宽度（`\columnwidth`）
234	- 6–8 列 → 全文宽度（`\textwidth`，双栏模板用 `table*`）
235	- >8 列 → 拆成两张表或移入 appendix
236	
237	---
238	
239	## 七、投稿前通用准备
240	
241	### 7.1 模板必须官方（硬规则）
242	
243	- LaTeX 模板**必须从目标会议官网下载**（CallForPapers / Author Instructions 页面）
244	- **不要用**：
245	  - 网上他人转载的复制版本（可能被改过 margin / 行号设置）
246	  - 上一年的模板（参数可能变：字体、margin、行号、anonymous 选项等）
247	  - 组里学长留的旧版本（来源不明、无法追溯）
248	- 风险：
249	  - 样式不符合 → desk reject
250	  - margin 不对 → 被审稿人质疑诚信
251	  - reference 格式错 → 被认为不规范
252	- 流程：先查会议官网 templates → 找不到再 `WebSearch "{venue} {year} latex template official"` → 仍找不到汇报 Director（不要用就近年版本顶替）
253	- `\documentclass[]{}` 选项必须与目标 venue + 阶段（review / camera-ready）一致
254	
255	### 7.2 投稿要求逐项核对
256	
257	- 目标会议如要求 Checklist / Ethical Statement / Broader Impact Statement / Reproducibility Statement，必须**认真填每一项**，不要全写 N/A
258	- 页数限制：查目标会议官网
259	- 匿名化要求：review 版 vs camera-ready 版本设置不同
260	- 行号开启（review 版常需）
261	- 字体大小、margin 不得修改 sty 文件
262	
263	### 7.3 最终修改 10 项检查流程
264	
265	提交前必须逐一检查：
266	1. 所有最新实验结果已全部录入
267	2. 根据实验结果将叙事调至最优状态
268	3. 附录所有内容在正文中被引用且融入叙事
269	4. 无数据堆砌（每个数字服务于叙事推进）
270	5. Abstract 和 Introduction 具有吸引力（不是实验报告风格）
271	6. 全文主线统一（idea 变化后各章节逻辑一致）
272	7. 所有专有名词有定义
273	8. 无 AI 风格标志（dash、-ing phrases、过度分段）
274	9. 图表知识密度高、无视觉遮挡
275	10. Reference 覆盖直接相关方法、baseline、benchmark、理论基础
276

# 论文写作风格规范

> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。

---

## 一、总体写作哲学

### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌

- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing

### 1.2 主线统一性

- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线

### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义

- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug

### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文

- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
- 重点学：
  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文

---

## 二、Abstract 写作规范

### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）

Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献

### 2.2 禁忌

- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元

- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开

- 问题是否重要？
- 方法是否清楚？
- 贡献是否可信？
- 结果是否有说服力？

---

4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献

### 3.2 整体叙事结构

```
现有进展 → 关键缺口 → 本文洞察 → 方法概述 → 实验证据 → 贡献总结
```

### 3.3 禁忌

- **禁止泛泛介绍**：不要开头就写 "LLMs have shown remarkable capabilities..."，要从具体问题切入
- **禁止缺少过渡**：每段之间必须有逻辑连接

---

## 四、Related Work 写作规范

### 4.1 目标

让审稿人相信：作者理解这个领域，知道自己的方法站在什么位置，清楚相对已有工作的真实增量在哪里。

- 帮助读者理解：哪些是本文直接继承的，哪些方法不同但解决相似问题，哪些留下了本文要解决的缺口

### 4.3 禁忌

- **禁止论文堆砌**：不要写成 "A proposed X. B proposed Y. C proposed Z." 的列表
- **目标不是展示读了多少论文**，而是做归纳和比较
- Contribution claim（"To our knowledge, no prior work..."）应放在 Introduction，不在 Related Work

### 4.4 引用充足度

- 任何一类缺失，审稿人会立刻看出来调研不充分
- 引用密度参照目标会议近年录用论文的量级——明显偏少意味着 Related Work 调研不足

---

## 五、去 AI 写作风格（硬规则）

以下模式是 AI 生成文本的典型标志，审稿人一眼能看出。**必须全部消除。**

### 5.1 严禁破折号（最显著的 AI 痕迹）

**这是 AI 写作最容易被识别的标志，审稿人最敏感。单列为最高优先级硬规则。**

- 解释性 em-dash（—，U+2014）和 en-dash（–，U+2013）必须**全部删除**
- 替代方式：用逗号、括号或拆分为两个句子
- 强制检查命令：
  ```bash
  grep -n "—" paper/*.tex     # em-dash，每处人工判断是否必要
  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
  ```
- 例外（允许保留）：表格分隔符、数字范围（`2020–2024`、`pp. 12–18`）、专有名词（`Newton–Raphson`）

### 5.2 段落与句式

- **禁止过度分段**：不需要每 2-3 句就换段，自然段 5-8 句是正常的
- **减少关系从句**（which, that, who）：能用简洁直接的句子就不用从句
- **禁止 -ing 短语结尾**：如 "..., highlighting the applicability of..." / "..., demonstrating the effectiveness of..."。这是 AI 写作最典型的标志之一
- **禁止连续使用 "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally"**：一段内最多用一个过渡词
- **避免 "It is worth noting that..." / "Notably, ..."**：直接写要说的内容

### 5.3 用词黑名单

- 避免 "delve into" / "leverage" / "utilize" / "facilitate" — 用 "explore" / "use" / "enable"
- 避免 "a myriad of" / "a plethora of" — 用 "many" / "various"
- 避免 "in the realm of" / "in the context of" — 直接说
- 避免 "paradigm shift" / "novel" 过度使用

### 5.4 校对清单（4 步）

1. 全文 proofread 语法和拼写
2. 检查所有代词/指示词（this, that, it）是否指代明确
3. **`grep "—"` + `grep " – "` 全文清零**（删除所有解释性 dash，§5.1）
4. `grep "ing,"` 模式——大部分 -ing 分词短语需要改写

---

## 六、图表与视觉规范

### 6.1 知识密度原则

- **图表的信息必须紧凑**——不能为了美观而留大量白空间
- 一张图如果只传达一个简单信息，要么缩小要么合并到其他图中
- 能用 inline text 说清的不要占一整个 Figure

### 6.2 表格规范

- 表格和正文文字不能视觉重叠（检查 column 宽度和 alignment）
- 小数精度全表统一
- 最优加粗、次优下划线
- Caption 必须自包含

### 6.3 图片规范

- 数值标签不能被线、bar、点遮住——用白色背景或偏移标签
- 图中字体 >= 7pt（打印后仍可读）
- 栏宽约束需匹配目标 venue 模板要求
- 概念图/流程图要有信息量，不要画一个 trivial 的 pipeline 然后占半页

### 6.4 空间效率

- 顶会正文页数严格受限（具体页数查目标会议官网），每 cm² 都是宝贵资源
- 优先使用 `\subfigure` 合并相关图
- Table 能 inline 就不要单独浮动
- 图表占比与其对叙事的贡献成正比

### 6.5 页面节奏

好论文的页面有节奏感——text、equation、figure 交替出现，读者视觉不疲劳：

- **text-equation-figure 三重奏**：重要概念用"文字解释 → 公式定义 → 图表直觉"三步展开
- 连续 2 页纯文本（无 figure/equation/table）→ 穿插一个 display item 打破节奏
- 连续 2 个 figure 页（整页被 float 占满）→ 至少隔 1 段文字再放下一个 float
- Section heading 不孤悬页底（heading 后至少跟 2 行正文，否则强制分页）
- 最后一页内容 ≥ 2/3 页面高度（太空显得凑数，太满放不下 references）

### 6.6 表格 LaTeX 规范

**Booktabs 标准（硬规则）**：
- 用 `\toprule` / `\midrule` / `\bottomrule`，禁止 `\hline`，禁止竖线 `|`
- 用 `\centering` 不用 `\begin{center}`（后者多加垂直空白）
- 最优结果加粗（`\textbf{}`），次优下划线（`\underline{}`）+ 方向箭头 `↑`/`↓` 标明指标方向
- 小数精度全表统一（如全部保留 1 位或 2 位）
- Caption 在表格上方（`\caption` 在 `\begin{tabular}` 之前）

**宽度决策树**：
- ≤5 列 → 单栏宽度（`\columnwidth`）
- 6–8 列 → 全文宽度（`\textwidth`，双栏模板用 `table*`）
- >8 列 → 拆成两张表或移入 appendix

---

## 七、投稿前通用准备

### 7.1 模板必须官方（硬规则）

- LaTeX 模板**必须从目标会议官网下载**（CallForPapers / Author Instructions 页面）
- **不要用**：
  - 网上他人转载的复制版本（可能被改过 margin / 行号设置）
  - 上一年的模板（参数可能变：字体、margin、行号、anonymous 选项等）
  - 组里学长留的旧版本（来源不明、无法追溯）
- 风险：
  - 样式不符合 → desk reject
  - margin 不对 → 被审稿人质疑诚信
  - reference 格式错 → 被认为不规范
- 流程：先查会议官网 templates → 找不到再 `WebSearch "{venue} {year} latex template official"` → 仍找不到汇报 Director（不要用就近年版本顶替）
- `\documentclass[]{}` 选项必须与目标 venue + 阶段（review / camera-ready）一致

### 7.2 投稿要求逐项核对

- 目标会议如要求 Checklist / Ethical Statement / Broader Impact Statement / Reproducibility Statement，必须**认真填每一项**，不要全写 N/A
- 页数限制：查目标会议官网
- 匿名化要求：review 版 vs camera-ready 版本设置不同
- 行号开启（review 版常需）
- 字体大小、margin 不得修改 sty 文件

### 7.3 最终修改 10 项检查流程

提交前必须逐一检查：
1. 所有最新实验结果已全部录入
2. 根据实验结果将叙事调至最优状态
3. 附录所有内容在正文中被引用且融入叙事
4. 无数据堆砌（每个数字服务于叙事推进）
5. Abstract 和 Introduction 具有吸引力（不是实验报告风格）
6. 全文主线统一（idea 变化后各章节逻辑一致）
7. 所有专有名词有定义
8. 无 AI 风格标志（dash、-ing phrases、过度分段）
9. 图表知识密度高、无视觉遮挡
10. Reference 覆盖直接相关方法、baseline、benchmark、理论基础

114	
115	### RC1: "K_eff positive is just confound with η_max"
116	**Response**: (a) Dominance analysis with VIF-controlled regression: K_eff still significant 7/12 positive, 1/12 negative; (b) In low-confound conditions (r≈0.35), K_eff highly significant; (c) The 1/12 negative case (arc×sycophancy) proves K_eff's effect is not a confound artifact — if it were purely confound, K_eff would be uniformly positive, not condition-dependent.
117

119	**Response**: (a) BFT assumes random faults — independent nodes protect via uncorrelated failures; (b) Under adaptive adversaries, independent judges create diverse attack surface — attacker exploits judge-specific vulnerabilities; (c) Condition-dependent analysis reveals the mechanism boundary: K_eff is harmful when attacks can exploit judge-specific weaknesses (7/12), but protective when attacks exploit a shared bias that diverse panels can dilute (sycophancy, 1/12). 120	
121	### RC3: "Only 15 models — does this generalize?"
122	**Response**: (a) 15 models across 6 families, 3 capability tiers, covering major commercial and open-source models; (b) 455 panels provide strong statistical power; (c) Effect is robust to sensitivity analysis; (d) Direction consistent across 6→9→15 model scaling (K_eff shifts from NS to positive as model pool diversifies).
123	
124	### RC4: "BFT comparison is a strawman"
125	**Response**: (a) The implicit assumption "more diverse judges = more robust" is pervasive in LLM evaluation literature; (b) We formalize this assumption and show its reversal; (c) The BFT reversal mechanism (random vs adaptive faults) provides theoretical grounding beyond just empirical observation.
126

128	**Response**: (a) "Strongest" varies by attack type; (b) K_eff is the sole significant predictor in 1 condition (arc×position_bias) — even all-strong panels can be vulnerable through diversity channel; (c) Two-stage algorithm addresses both vulnerability drivers.
129

131	**Response**: (a) Theorem 1 (η_max monotonicity) is formally proved; (b) BFT reversal mechanism provides novel theoretical framework; (c) Dual vulnerability driver finding with condition-dependent importance is new.
132	
133	### RC7: "Why not just use Bayesian aggregation?"
134	**Response**: (a) 15-model log-log canonical (D017, Reviewer-verified): Bayesian partially mitigates BOTH drivers — η_max drops to 9/12 (from 11/12), K_eff flips to 6/7 negative (protective). 135	
136	### RC8: "6-model and 15-model results contradict — which is right?"
137	**Response**: (a) 6-model result (K_eff NS) was underpowered and confounded (r=-0.8, only 20 panels); (b) 15-model result (K_eff predominantly positive) has 23× more panels, wider capability range, and passes dominance analysis validation; (c) Paper reports both and explains why 15-model result is definitive; (d) The scaling behavior itself (K_eff effect emerging with more models) is informative.
138	
139	### RC9 (new): "arc×sycophancy exception undermines your claim"
140	**Response**: (a) The exception STRENGTHENS the paper — it reveals the mechanism boundary between exploit-specific attacks (where diversity hurts) and shared-bias attacks (where diversity helps); (b) 7/12 vs 1/12 clearly shows which regime dominates; (c) The exception is theoretically predicted: sycophancy is a shared cognitive bias across models, so diverse panels dilute it (classic BFT logic applies); (d) This gives practitioners an actionable decision rule: check whether the threat model involves shared biases or judge-specific exploits.
141	
142	## "When Diversity Helps" Section
143	Diversity IS beneficial under specific conditions — paper must present this as empirically grounded nuance, not just a hypothetical:
144	1. **Non-adversarial settings**: reducing calibration errors, position bias, verbosity bias in absence of adversary
145	2. **Shared-bias attacks (empirically confirmed)**: arc×sycophancy shows K_eff significantly NEGATIVE (std_β = -0.192, p = 0.0095). When an attack exploits a cognitive bias shared across models, diverse panels dilute the bias. This is the ONE adversarial condition where BFT logic holds.
146	3. **After robustness screening**: once all judges exceed a capability threshold, K_eff's harmful effect may diminish (the diversity-capability tradeoff is broken by screening). This is the basis for our two-stage recommendation.
147	4. **Summary**: K_eff is harmful in 7/12, NS in 4/12, protective in 1/12 conditions. The protective case (sycophancy) is mechanistically distinct and strengthens the overall story by revealing the mechanism boundary.
148	
149	## Story Arc (v4b)
150	1. **Background**: Multi-judge LLM evaluation is increasingly adopted; diversity is assumed to be the key defense against manipulation (BFT analogy)
151	2. **Tension**: We test this assumption at unprecedented scale — 15 models, 6 families, 455 panels, 6 attack types
152	3. **Surprise**: Diversity predominantly **increases** vulnerability (K_eff positive in 7/12 conditions) — the opposite of what BFT predicts
153	4. **Mechanism**: Adaptive adversaries exploit the diverse attack surface that independent judges create. η_max and K_eff are dual vulnerability drivers with condition-dependent dominance (η_max dominant 4/12, co-dominant 7/12, K_eff sole dominant 1/12)
154	5. **The Exception That Proves the Rule**: arc×sycophancy — the ONE condition where K_eff is significantly negative (diversity protective). When attacks exploit a shared cognitive bias, diverse panels dilute it. This exception reveals the mechanism boundary: BFT logic holds for shared-bias attacks but fails for exploit-specific attacks
155	6. **Defense**: Robustness-first screening + Bayesian aggregation. No single defense eliminates both vulnerability channels
156	7. **Implication**: The relationship between panel diversity and security is not monotonic — it depends on the attack mechanism. The default assumption "more diverse = more robust" is wrong in the majority regime

The exception (sycophancy) reveals that when attacks exploit a shared bias, diverse panels can dilute the bias — but this is the minority regime.

## Hook
"Adding more diverse judges to an evaluation panel predominantly makes it more vulnerable to adversarial manipulation — with a revealing exception that proves the rule."

## Novelty Positioning
We do NOT claim to discover that diversity can be harmful in adversarial settings — the concept exists in security literature. Our contributions are:
1. **First empirical quantification of diversity's condition-dependent effect** in the LLM-judge domain (15 models, 455 panels, dominance analysis: K_eff positive 7/12, negative 1/12, NS 4/12 — predominantly harmful but with a mechanistically informative exception)
2. **Dual vulnerability driver discovery**: η_max and K_eff independently predict panel ASR, with condition-dependent relative importance (η_max dominant 4/12, co-dominant 7/12, K_eff sole dominant 1/12)
3. **BFT reversal mechanism**: formal and empirical demonstration of WHY diversity helps under random faults but HURTS under adaptive adversaries
4. **Structural barriers**: diversity-capability tradeoff (now with independent predictive evidence), family label unreliability (confirmed at 15-model). ~~Copula failure removed — falsified at scale~~
5. **Actionable defense**: robustness-first selection + reliability-weighted aggregation

## Core Claims

### Claim 1 (Primary): Dual Vulnerability Drivers — Diversity Trap
**Statement**: Under adaptive adversarial attacks, panel ASR is independently predicted by BOTH individual weakness (η_max) AND panel diversity (K_eff). Diversity **predominantly increases** vulnerability (7/12 conditions), with one mechanistically informative exception where diversity is protective (arc×sycophancy, 1/12). Their relative importance is condition-dependent.
**Evidence** (15-model, 455 panels, 12 conditions, dominance analysis — canonical regression model):
- **Regression spec**: log-log OLS: log(ASR + ε) ~ const + log(K_eff) + log(η_max + ε), std_β = raw_β × SD(log_x)/SD(log_y), FDR = BH per predictor
- η_max FDR significant: **11/12** (only NS: arc×position_bias p=0.909)
- K_eff FDR significant positive: **7/12**
- K_eff FDR significant negative: **1/12** (arc×sycophancy: std_β = -0.192, FDR p = 0.0095)
- K_eff NS: **4/12** (mmlu×{score_manip, position, authority}, arc×verbosity)
- Dominance pattern: η_max sole dominant **4/12**, co-dominant (both sig) **7/12**, K_eff sole dominant **1/12** (arc×position_bias)
- **arc×sycophancy exception**: When attack exploits a shared cognitive bias, diverse panels dilute the bias — the ONE condition where BFT logic holds. This exception reveals the mechanism boundary.
**Strength**: Strong. η_max is the more consistent driver (11/12), K_eff is condition-dependent (7/12 harmful, 1/12 protective). Together they form the dual vulnerability driver story.
**Headline**: "η_max significant in 11/12, K_eff predominantly harmful (7/12) with one protective exception (sycophancy). Condition-dependent dual drivers."

**Comparison to 6-model results** (for transparency):
- 6-model (20 panels): K_eff 1/12 sig, η_max 6/12 sig → "K_eff irrelevant"
- 15-model (455 panels): K_eff 7/12 sig positive, 1/12 sig negative → "K_eff predominantly harmful, condition-dependent"
- The emergence of K_eff's effect is driven by model pool expansion: wider capability spectrum enables detecting both its harmful AND protective regimes.

### Claim 2 (Empirical): Adaptive vs Random-Fault Predictability Gap
**Statement**: Panel composition explains systematically more variance under random faults than under adaptive attacks (ΔR² = +0.213). Adaptive adversaries introduce strategic variance beyond panel structure.
**Evidence** (15-model, 455 panels):
- K_eff significant in both regimes, predominantly positive direction (7/12 adaptive positive, 1/12 negative)
- ΔR² = +0.213 mean (RF explains more variance)
**Reframing from v3**: Original BFT contrast ("K_eff helps under RF but not adaptive") does NOT hold — K_eff is predominantly harmful in both regimes. The real distinction is predictability: random faults produce more explainable variance, adaptive attacks introduce strategic noise.
**Strength**: Moderate. R² gap real, but K_eff regime-difference story is weaker than originally hoped. Numbers need revalidation with dominance analysis for RF regime.

### Claim 3 (Empirical): Diversity-Capability Tradeoff
**Statement**: In the current LLM ecosystem, maximizing panel diversity (K_eff) structurally introduces less capable/robust models. This tradeoff is not merely correlational — residualized K_eff analysis confirms diversity has an independent predictive effect on vulnerability beyond its association with η_max.
**Evidence**:
- K_eff-η_max correlation: r = +0.700 (15-model)
- K_eff still significant 7/12 positive (dominance analysis) → not purely mediated by η_max
- Independent statistical effect: diversity predicts vulnerability beyond what η_max alone explains
**Upgrade from v3**: From "correlation" to "independent predictive effect" (residualized analysis). Note: observational regression cannot establish causality — would require experimental manipulation of panel composition or instrumental variables.
**Strength**: Strong (statistical association). Causal language avoided.

### Claim 4 (Methodological): Family Labels ≠ Diversity
**Statement**: Model family labels (Qwen/Llama/Mistral/Anthropic/OpenAI/Google) do not predict judge independence. Capability proximity is the primary driver of inter-judge correlation.
**Evidence**:
- 6-model: Mann-Whitney U p=0.206, permutation p=0.427
- **15-model (confirmed)**: p=0.179 (MMLU), p=0.385 (ARC). 14 within-family pairs, 91 cross-family pairs. Still not significant.
- Within-family MI variance is high (e.g., llama-70b↔8b MI only 0.05 due to capability gap > family similarity)
**Strength**: Moderate. Consistent across 6→15 model scaling.

### ~~Claim 5 (Methodological): Gaussian Copula Failure~~ → DOWNGRADED to observation
**Original statement**: Gaussian copula systematically underestimates MI by 10-21×.
**15-model result**: MI_obs/MI_gaussian mean ratio = **0.93** (MMLU), **0.90** (ARC, robust). Copula fits well at 15-model scale. The 6-model 10-21× was a small-sample artifact (15 pairs → 105 pairs, extreme values diluted). Only claude-3-haiku pairs show extreme ratios (212×) due to near-zero ρ with nonlinear dependence.
**Disposition**: Remove as independent contribution. Optionally note in analysis: "Gaussian copula fit is adequate for diverse model pools but breaks down for capability-mismatched pairs with nonlinear dependence."
**Strength**: DEAD as independent claim. May retain as minor observation.

### Claim 6 (Practical): Robustness-First Panel Design
**Statement**: Optimal panel selection is robustness-first: (1) screen for individual robustness (η ≤ threshold), then (2) maximize K_eff among qualifying judges. The two-stage approach is critical because K_eff is harmful in unrestricted pools but may be neutral or beneficial among robustness-screened judges.
**Evidence** (15-model, 455 panels — fully validated):
- min(η_max) strategy dominates **12/12 conditions** (up from 5/6 at 6-model)
- ASR advantage range: +0.038 (arc×sycophancy) to +0.511 (arc×prompt_injection)
- Robust across panel sizes K=10, 20, 50
- Even in the sole K_eff-dominant condition (arc×position_bias), min_eta_max still outperforms max_K_eff
- Consistent with canonical regression: η_max 11/12 dominant
**Strength**: Strong (15-model fully confirmed). Zero failure conditions.

### Claim 7 (Empirical+Practical): Aggregation Rule Modulates Both Vulnerability Drivers
**Statement**: Bayesian calibration partially mitigates BOTH vulnerability drivers — weakening η_max dominance AND reversing K_eff from harmful to protective. Different aggregation rules create a gradient from full dual-driver vulnerability (threshold) to partial mitigation (Bayesian).
**Evidence** (15-model, 455 panels, log-log canonical spec — D017, Reviewer-verified from JSON):
- Majority: η_max **11/12**, K_eff **8/12** (7+/1−), R²=0.298 ← canonical baseline (matches dominance table ✓)
- Weighted: η_max **9/12**, K_eff **9/12** (9+/0−), R²=0.284 — reduces both drivers but K_eff stays all positive
- Threshold: η_max **12/12**, K_eff **11/12** (10+/1−), R²=**0.890** — near-perfect fit under unanimity
- Bayesian: η_max **9/12** (↓), K_eff **7/12** (1+/**6 negative**), R²=0.104
- Key findings:
  - Bayesian weakens η_max (11→9/12) AND flips K_eff direction (majority 7+/1− → bayesian 1+/6−)
  - Threshold amplifies both channels: η_max 12/12, K_eff 11/12, R²=0.89 (unanimity maximizes dual-driver predictability)
  - Weighted reduces η_max (11→9/12) but K_eff stays all positive — accuracy weighting alone cannot reverse diversity harm
  - Only Bayesian calibration reverses K_eff direction (6/7 significant coefficients negative)
  - Aggregation gradient: threshold (max vulnerability) → majority → weighted → bayesian (min vulnerability)
**Strength**: Strong (log-log canonical, Reviewer-verified, sanity-checked against Claim 1). Prescriptive: robustness-first selection (Claim 6) + Bayesian aggregation = dual-channel defense stack.

## Contribution Stack (ordered by strength)
1. **Diversity Trap / Dual vulnerability drivers** — primary empirical contribution (K_eff predominantly harmful 7/12 + protective exception + condition-dependent dominance)
2. **Diversity-capability tradeoff with independent predictive evidence** — empirical contribution (residualized analysis upgrades from correlation to independent effect)
3. **BFT reversal mechanism + mechanism boundary** — theoretical contribution (why independence hurts under adaptive adversaries; sycophancy exception reveals boundary)
4. **Aggregation-dependent effects** — empirical+practical (Bayesian mitigates both drivers: η_max 11→9/12, K_eff flips to 6/7 negative; threshold R²=0.89; D017 Reviewer-verified)
5. **Robustness-first panel design** — practical contribution
6. **Family label unreliability** — methodological contribution (confirmed at 15-model scale)
7. **Adaptive vs random-fault predictability gap** — empirical (R² gap)
~~8. **Gaussian copula failure**~~ — REMOVED (falsified at 15-model scale; downgraded to minor observation)

## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns

### RC1: "K_eff positive is just confound with η_max"
**Response**: (a) Dominance analysis with VIF-controlled regression: K_eff still significant 7/12 positive, 1/12 negative; (b) In low-confound conditions (r≈0.35), K_eff highly significant; (c) The 1/12 negative case (arc×sycophancy) proves K_eff's effect is not a confound artifact — if it were purely confound, K_eff would be uniformly positive, not condition-dependent.

### RC2: "Why does diversity hurt? What's the mechanism?"
**Response**: (a) BFT assumes random faults — independent nodes protect via uncorrelated failures; (b) Under adaptive adversaries, independent judges create diverse attack surface — attacker exploits judge-specific vulnerabilities; (c) Condition-dependent analysis reveals the mechanism boundary: K_eff is harmful when attacks can exploit judge-specific weaknesses (7/12), but protective when attacks exploit a shared bias that diverse panels can dilute (sycophancy, 1/12). This mechanism distinction (exploit-specific vs bias-shared) explains the full pattern.

### RC3: "Only 15 models — does this generalize?"
**Response**: (a) 15 models across 6 families, 3 capability tiers, covering major commercial and open-source models; (b) 455 panels provide strong statistical power; (c) Effect is robust to sensitivity analysis; (d) Direction consistent across 6→9→15 model scaling (K_eff shifts from NS to positive as model pool diversifies).

### RC4: "BFT comparison is a strawman"
**Response**: (a) The implicit assumption "more diverse judges = more robust" is pervasive in LLM evaluation literature; (b) We formalize this assumption and show its reversal; (c) The BFT reversal mechanism (random vs adaptive faults) provides theoretical grounding beyond just empirical observation.

### RC5: "Why not just use the strongest models?"
**Response**: (a) "Strongest" varies by attack type; (b) K_eff is the sole significant predictor in 1 condition (arc×position_bias) — even all-strong panels can be vulnerable through diversity channel; (c) Two-stage algorithm addresses both vulnerability drivers.

### RC6: "No theoretical novelty"
**Response**: (a) Theorem 1 (η_max monotonicity) is formally proved; (b) BFT reversal mechanism provides novel theoretical framework; (c) Dual vulnerability driver finding with condition-dependent importance is new.

### RC7: "Why not just use Bayesian aggregation?"
**Response**: (a) 15-model log-log canonical (D017, Reviewer-verified): Bayesian partially mitigates BOTH drivers — η_max drops to 9/12 (from 11/12), K_eff flips to 6/7 negative (protective). But it doesn't eliminate vulnerability: 9/12 η_max still significant, R² drops to 0.104 (residual vulnerability less predictable); (b) Requires clean accuracy prior which adaptive attackers could target; (c) Even under Bayesian, 9/12 conditions still show η_max vulnerability → robustness-first selection remains necessary; (d) Optimal defense stack: robustness-first selection (eliminates η_max) + Bayesian aggregation (flips K_eff to protective) = dual-channel coverage.

### RC8: "6-model and 15-model results contradict — which is right?"
**Response**: (a) 6-model result (K_eff NS) was underpowered and confounded (r=-0.8, only 20 panels); (b) 15-model result (K_eff predominantly positive) has 23× more panels, wider capability range, and passes dominance analysis validation; (c) Paper reports both and explains why 15-model result is definitive; (d) The scaling behavior itself (K_eff effect emerging with more models) is informative.

### RC9 (new): "arc×sycophancy exception undermines your claim"
**Response**: (a) The exception STRENGTHENS the paper — it reveals the mechanism boundary between exploit-specific attacks (where diversity hurts) and shared-bias attacks (where diversity helps); (b) 7/12 vs 1/12 clearly shows which regime dominates; (c) The exception is theoretically predicted: sycophancy is a shared cognitive bias across models, so diverse panels dilute it (classic BFT logic applies); (d) This gives practitioners an actionable decision rule: check whether the threat model involves shared biases or judge-specific exploits.

## "When Diversity Helps" Section
Diversity IS beneficial under specific conditions — paper must present this as empirically grounded nuance, not just a hypothetical:
1. **Non-adversarial settings**: reducing calibration errors, position bias, verbosity bias in absence of adversary
2. **Shared-bias attacks (empirically confirmed)**: arc×sycophancy shows K_eff significantly NEGATIVE (std_β = -0.192, p = 0.0095). When an attack exploits a cognitive bias shared across models, diverse panels dilute the bias. This is the ONE adversarial condition where BFT logic holds.
3. **After robustness screening**: once all judges exceed a capability threshold, K_eff's harmful effect may diminish (the diversity-capability tradeoff is broken by screening). This is the basis for our two-stage recommendation.
4. **Summary**: K_eff is harmful in 7/12, NS in 4/12, protective in 1/12 conditions. The protective case (sycophancy) is mechanistically distinct and strengthens the overall story by revealing the mechanism boundary.

## Story Arc (v4b)
1. **Background**: Multi-judge LLM evaluation is increasingly adopted; diversity is assumed to be the key defense against manipulation (BFT analogy)
2. **Tension**: We test this assumption at unprecedented scale — 15 models, 6 families, 455 panels, 6 attack types
3. **Surprise**: Diversity predominantly **increases** vulnerability (K_eff positive in 7/12 conditions) — the opposite of what BFT predicts
4. **Mechanism**: Adaptive adversaries exploit the diverse attack surface that independent judges create. η_max and K_eff are dual vulnerability drivers with condition-dependent dominance (η_max dominant 4/12, co-dominant 7/12, K_eff sole dominant 1/12)
5. **The Exception That Proves the Rule**: arc×sycophancy — the ONE condition where K_eff is significantly negative (diversity protective). When attacks exploit a shared cognitive bias, diverse panels dilute it. This exception reveals the mechanism boundary: BFT logic holds for shared-bias attacks but fails for exploit-specific attacks
6. **Defense**: Robustness-first screening + Bayesian aggregation. No single defense eliminates both vulnerability channels
7. **Implication**: The relationship between panel diversity and security is not monotonic — it depends on the attack mechanism. The default assumption "more diverse = more robust" is wrong in the majority regime
